historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission let a $498.50 contract to demolish two temporary buildings standing in Portsmouth Square, a theater building and a custom house building.

The Recreation and Park Commission let the California State Park Commission put a memorial plaque to Andrew S. Hallidie, inventor of the cable car, in Portsmouth Square, at the eastern terminus of the Clay Street Hill Railroad, opened in August 1873.

After a hearing at which some speakers objected to its effect on the children's play area, the Recreation and Park Commission approved in principle the Redevelopment Agency's plan for a pedestrian bridge over Kearny Street from the Chinese Cultural Center to Portsmouth Square, on condition that the developer, Justice Enterprises, move the children's area at its own cost; the bridge, presented in September by the architect Clement Chen, Jr., was part of a building with a 27-story hotel and the Chinese Cultural and Trade Center.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved the schematic plan for the second phase of Portsmouth Square's master plan, covering the upper plaza: raised planters with benches around its edge, 64 new trees, light gray granite paving, and restoration of the schoolhouse monument, the Stevenson monument and the plaza's other monuments, with construction hoped for in early 1992.
